learning_outcomes.text: Compute the probability of an event
Model nondeterministic characteristics using random variables and their distributions
Analyse samples and interpret the results
Compute estimates for the mean and variance of a population and for a proportion
Obtain the confidence intervals for the mean and variance of a population and for a proportion
Design hypothesis tests for the mean and variance of a population and for a proportion
Assess the compatibility of a sample with a statistical model using adjustment tests
Use the notion of p-value in statistical software

syllabus_topics: Probabilities: Kolmogorov probability definition and its consequences. Conditional probability. Independence of events.

Random variables and distributions: continuous and discrete real random variables. Discrete and continuous probabilistic models. Multidimensional distributions. Central Limit Theorem and applications.
Point and interval estimation of parameters.
Hypothesis tests: Parametric tests. Adjustment tests. Independence tests.
assessment_rules: Assessment can be done either through continuous assessment (2 or more midterm exams) or through a final assessment exam. Both continuous and final assessment methods are weighted at 100%.
